questions.q: What does position (not name) match in an INSERT INTO ... VALUES statement?
options: Each value in the VALUES list to the column at the same position in the column list
Each value to the column with the same data type
Each value to the first NULL-able column available
Each value to a column chosen alphabetically
questions.explain: The first value lines up with the first column in the column list, the second value with the second column, and so on by position.

questions.q: Why is it safer to always list column names explicitly in an INSERT statement?
options: It protects the statement from breaking if the table's column order changes or a column is added later
It makes the statement run faster
SQL Server requires it for IDENTITY columns
It is required whenever a column allows NULL
questions.explain: Omitting the column list relies on the table's exact current column order, which is fragile if the table is later altered.

questions.q: Why does ProductID never appear in the INSERT statements against dbo.LessonDemo?
options: It's an IDENTITY column, so SQL Server assigns its value automatically
It was declared NULL-able so it can be skipped
VARCHAR columns must always come first
INSERT statements can never reference primary key columns
questions.explain: IDENTITY(1,1) tells SQL Server to generate the next value itself — you must not supply one.

options: The last identity value generated in the current session
The total row count in the table
The column list of the most recent insert
The default value of the most recently altered column
questions.explain: SCOPE_IDENTITY() lets you retrieve the auto-generated identity value right after an insert, within the same scope.

questions.q: Why does 'INSERT INTO dbo.LessonDemo (ProductName, Color) VALUES ('Test', 'Red');' fail?
options: ListPrice is NOT NULL and has no default, so it must be supplied
ProductName must always be the last column listed
Color cannot be inserted without ProductID
VALUES can only be used with numeric columns
questions.explain: Any NOT NULL column without a default must receive a value in the INSERT, or the statement fails a constraint check.
